en.title: Sum of Shortest Distances for Multiple Ring Trips
en.description:
distances[i] connects station i and station (i+1) modulo n. Each query is an independent start and end; take the shorter of the clockwise and counterclockwise distances, then sum over all queries.

The standard I/O and the solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n q, the second line contains n edge lengths, followed by q lines of 0-based start and end stations. The original gives no value ranges; this site sets 1≤n,q≤100000, 1≤(edge length)≤10⁹.
en.explanation: Example 1: the shortest distances are 1, 5 and 4, for a total of 10. Example 2: 0 to 2 goes the other way for 13, and 2 to 1 is 10, for a total of 23. Example 3: the same station needs no movement, for a total of 0.
hints: Prefix sums give the distance d in the linear unrolling, and the shortest distance on the ring is min(d,perimeter−d); add it up query by query.
